both for live play and ScriptedInput
Every field is private and there are no setters.
lockedPriceCents is final: the price is fixed when the order
is taken. status changes only through advancePreparation,
markServed, markPaid and cancel, and each one throws
IllegalStateException when called out of order.
Restaurant creates its Tables (from tableCount) and its
WaitingQueue itself, so they exist only inside it: filled
diamonds. The Menu and the three staff members are
created in RestaurantRush and passed to the constructor,
which makes those aggregations: hollow diamonds.
Customer is abstract. applyWaitingLoss() calls the abstract
its own amount per turn (Regular 8, VIP 5, Critic 12).
and satisfactionToRecord(). Stage 2 added both without

association: navigable, the source holds a field
association: both ends hold a field
aggregation: whole holds parts made elsewhere
composition: whole creates and owns its parts
note (comment) joined to the class it describes
RestaurantRush (package app) only creates the objects and starts
the game, so it has no stereotype.
orange border: class added in stage 2
dashed orange border: class changed in stage 2
Visibility: + public, - private, # protected, ~ package. Underlined:
Constructor: the class name, and no return type
Every field, constructor and method declared in the code is listed.
{...} after an attribute is a constraint the class keeps.
Role names on the lines are the Java field names. {ordered}: the field
is a List, so it keeps its order.
Dependencies left out to keep lines apart
RestaurantRush creates and wires every object; only its «instantiate»
ArrivalSchedule creates the RegularCustomer, VIPCustomer and
CriticCustomer objects that it returns as Customer.
